answer: Shared-Resource Fingerprinting. Each identity must claim a disjoint slice of a public resource ledger—a unique random seed that a fable of prior transactions must reference. On every action, agents wander across peers that record the seed's usage thread; any seed seen under two identities is flagged. Duplication is self-revealing because two copies inevitably touch the same seed record, and the attacker must abandon a costly accumulated history per clone.
